_doc: Pin tables for the circuit check (kerf/circuit.py, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 'Circuit'). Key: a catalog path or a prefix of one (longest match wins). symbol: a KiCad symbol 'Lib:Name' from kicad-symbols (its pins, numbers and types are used); types: per-pin type overrides on a KiCad symbol whose generic pins are all passive (each needs types_why); pins: [[number, name, type], ...] for a part KiCad has no symbol for (types: input output bidirectional tristate passive power_in power_out open_collector). ports.out / ports.in: what a wiring run lands on - a port name ('' = a power run's default, 'signal' = a signal run's default, or the run's from/to '.port' suffix) maps to a pin list (one pin per conductor, + first for power) or to named instances {name: [pins]} chosen by the run's `pin:` or taken in order. optional: pins that may stay unconnected, with why (they get a KiCad no-connect flag; every other pin must be wired or the ERC fails). max_conductors: wires one pin/terminal takes. tied: groups of pins joined inside the part (one node). confidence 'role' = the pin names are the part's functional roles (power in, ground, video out, UART TX/RX) as the sources describe them, not pad labels read off the board.

servos.types_why: KiCad's generic Motor_Servo symbol marks all three pins passive; a hobby servo takes the PWM signal in and is powered through + / - (Pololu servo cable convention: 'brown or black = ground', 'orange, yellow, white, or blue = servo control signal line', red = power)
servos.source: https://www.pololu.com/product/2184 (servo cable colour convention, opened 2026-11-01); KiCad symbol Motor:Motor_Servo (kicad-symbols)

optional.why: OE is 'Pulled low by default' (outputs enabled); V+ is 'an optional power pin that will supply distributed power to the servos' that the chip does not use; unused PWM channels may stay open

boards.pca9685_adafruit.note: Pins tied together on the board are one pin here: the GND, VCC and V+ of both 6-pin side headers, the V+ terminal block and every port's V+ / GND row ('Each port has 3 pins: V+, GND and the PWM output'). PWM outputs have 220 ohm series resistors.
boards.pca9685_adafruit.source: https://learn.adafruit.com/16-channel-pwm-servo-driver/pinouts (opened 2026-11-01): GND 'must be connected'; VCC logic power 3-5 V; SCL/SDA 'weak pullup to VCC'; OE 'Pulled low by default'

optional.why: general-purpose I/O, the analog reference, the reset input (pulled up on the board), the 3.3 V output and VIN may stay open; the Nano can run from its USB port

boards.arduino_nano.note: A wire to a pin name lands on every symbol pin of that name (the two GND pins are tied on the board).
boards.arduino_nano.source: KiCad symbol MCU_Module:Arduino_Nano_v3.x (kicad-symbols): +5V power_out (the USB-fed 5 V rail), VIN/GND power_in, D/A pins bidirectional; https://docs.arduino.cc/resources/datasheets/A000005-datasheet.pdf

optional.why: second screw terminal of the same output (terminals 4-5 and 6-7 are tied inside the supply)

electronics.supplies.meanwell_lrs100_5.note: Terminals 5 and 7 are the second screw of the -V / +V outputs: passive here so one output is one driver (KiCad pin-type rules); a bootlace ferrule per terminal (one conductor each).
electronics.supplies.meanwell_lrs100_5.source: MEAN WELL LRS-100 datasheet, terminal pin assignment: 1 AC/L, 2 AC/N, 3 FG, 4-5 DC -V, 6-7 DC +V (catalog electronics.supplies.meanwell_lrs100_5 'terminals', https://www.power-supplies-australia.com.au/sites/default/files/specifications/MEAN%20WELL%20LRS-100%20DATA%20SHEET.pdf)

electronics.connectors.iec_inlet_fused_s.note: The inlet is where mains enters the circuit, so its switched/fused L and N tabs are the power source of the AC side; PE is the protective earth tab.
electronics.connectors.iec_inlet_fused_s.source: catalog electronics.connectors.iec_inlet_fused_switched_schurter_dd11 (L / N / PE tabs) and the electrical.mains jumpers (kerf/electrical.py)

electronics.connectors.wago_221_415.note: One item = the + and - splices (qty 2): each 221-415 joins 5 conductors (5 lever clamping units, all connected).

drone.batteries.types_why: KiCad's Device:Battery pins are passive; the pack is the source of the whole circuit, so both terminals drive their nets
drone.batteries.source: KiCad symbol Device:Battery (kicad-symbols); pack lead red + / black - to its XT60

drone.connectors.XT60.note: Pin_1 = + (the lead's red), Pin_2 = - : a plug passes both conductors straight through.
drone.connectors.XT60.source: KiCad symbol Connector_Generic:Conn_01x02 (kicad-symbols); KiCad footprint/3D AMASS_XT60-M_1x02_P7.2mm_Vertical (2 contacts)

optional.why: BEC outputs, video, UART and unused ESC outputs may stay open

drone.stacks.fc_30_5.note: FC + 4-in-1 ESC as one item: the ESC battery pads (BAT+, BAT- = GND) feed both boards; GND is common to every pad. Motor phases per ESC output (A/B/C order is arbitrary: swapping two reverses the motor).
drone.stacks.fc_30_5.source: https://ardupilot.org/plane/docs/common-speedybeef4-v3.html (SpeedyBee F405 V4: 'SERIAL2 -> UART2, RCIN', 'CRSF/ELRS ... T2', 'The CAM and VTX pins provide connections for using the internal OSD', '5V 2A BEC', '9V 2A for video', '4 in 1 ESC connector', M1-M4); https://www.speedybee.com/speedybee-f405-v4-bls-55a-30x30-fc-esc-stack/

drone.motors.source: three-phase brushless motor: three phase leads to one ESC output (catalog drone.motors source pages)

optional.why: IRC Tramp control from an FC UART TX is only needed to change channel / power from the FC (https://oscarliang.com/speedybee-tx800/: 'Connect the IRC wire/pad from the VTX to the TX pad of a spare UART')

drone.vtx.source: https://oscarliang.com/speedybee-tx800/ (opened 2026-11-01: 'Voltage input: 3.7-5.5V', IRC Tramp control); video in from the FC's VTX pad

optional.why: camera menu / UART control line, not needed to fly

drone.cameras.source: https://shop.runcam.com/runcam-phoenix-2/ (opened 2026-11-01: 'Power DC 5-36V', 6-pin FPV cable, menu/UART control)

electronics.receivers.elrs_nano.source: https://www.expresslrs.org/quick-start/receivers/wiring-up/ (opened 2026-11-01): 'The TX or T pad should be connected to an RX pad of the same UART number', 'The RX or R pad should be connected to a TX pad', VCC to a 5 V pad, GND to ground
